subject: P0: Regional fragmentation causing throughput failure — propose traffic quarantine and priority reroute
messages:
From: Claire Zhang <czhang@wakefieldhealth.com>
To: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Systems Ops <ops@elliotsys.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Spike: us-west-2 high latency + 502 bursts impacting batch ingest

Hi Ava,

We're seeing a sustained spike in tail latency and 502s from your API endpoints in us-west-2 starting ~08:50 PST. Our nightly batch jobs are failing (25% of batches now erroring) and interactive calls for a subset of our users are timing out. Attached is a screenshot of our metrics and a short sampling of error traces.

Key impact:
- Throughput dropped ~40% for our ingestion pipeline since 08:52.
- Error rate (5xx) up to 18% on /v1/generate for certain model routes.
- Customers on our West cluster reporting slower UI responses and occasional timeouts.

Can your team confirm whether there is a regional-level capacity / routing issue on Redwood's side? We need an ETA for mitigation — we may have to pause some downstream jobs if this persists.

Claire
Ops Lead, Wakefield Health
[attachment: p0_latency_graph.png (image/png)]

From: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <czhang@wakefieldhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-12T09:19:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike: us-west-2 high latency + 502 bursts impacting batch ingest

Hi Claire — I'm on it. Thanks for the graphs and traces. We're opening an internal P0 and pulling telemetry now. Can you also send a couple of request ids (X-Request-Id) from failing runs and the job ids that started at 08:45–09:00?

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Confirm if there is an AZ fragmentation or routing mesh failure in us-west-2.
2) Evaluate routing quarantine to push new requests to us-east-1 as a temporary mitigation.
3) If quarantine is feasible, perform a staged traffic shift and monitor error/latency.

I'll loop in our escalation lead (Marissa) for customer comms and exec coordination.

I'm available on ☎ now if you want to jump on a call.

— Ava
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[internal note: opened PD incident PD123456]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-12T09:33:00-08:00
Subject: URGENT: Wakefield P0 — propose "regional quarantine" to us-east-1 + priority routing pin

Team,

Wakefield is hitting major throughput and error pain in us-west-2. Ava, thanks for triage. We need to move fast — suggested plan below:

Proposed actions (requires exec approval for priority override):
- Execute regional quarantine: stop accepting new routed traffic into the affected us-west-2 routing mesh and route new requests for Wakefield to us-east-1 compatible clusters. (This is different from a full failover — it's a controlled quarantine to contain fragmentation.)
- Apply priority routing pin for Wakefield's account (temporary) to avoid normal load-balancing churn.
- Run quick health checks for stateful features (KV cache priming) to minimize cold-start latency.
- Push a one-paragraph customer comm acknowledging impact and mitigation in-flight.

Risks and notes:
- Cross-region traffic will increase egress and inter-region latency for some calls — expect a modest latency penalty but large error-rate improvement.
- If execute now, estimate 70–85% of traffic rerouted within 15 minutes, contingent on capacity in us-east-1.

Attachments: region_quarantine_runbook.pdf (excerpted runbook with required CLI steps). Ava: confirm capacity and any precheck requirements. Soojin: draft customer comm & credit proposal. Rishi/Vanessa: need sign-off to bypass standard change windows for priority pin and capacity borrow.

— Marissa
Account Escalation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-12T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Wakefield P0 — propose "regional quarantine" to us-east-1 + priority routing pin

All — quick update from ops: we've validated spare capacity in us-east-1 for the model family Wakefield runs (3x spare nodes in the high-memory pool). Ava confirmed runbook prechecks are green except for a small KV-cache warmup window.

Customer comm (draft):
Hi Claire — we detected a regional routing degradation in us-west-2 affecting a subset of your traffic. We've initiated an emergency traffic quarantine and are routing new requests to a healthy pool in us-east-1; you should see error rates and timeouts drop over the next 10–20 minutes. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary and a proposed credit.

Credit suggestion: 10% service credit for affected window + expedited SLO review.

Approvals needed:
- Rishi: approve temporary priority routing pin (bypass standard change controls).
- Vanessa: approve credit authorization and any billing adjustments.

If approved, I'll begin execution now and send step-by-step logs to the ticket.

— Soojin
Senior Incident Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: mitigation_log.txt (text)]

From: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <czhang@wakefieldhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-12T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike: us-west-2 high latency + 502 bursts impacting batch ingest — mitigation in flight

Claire — quick status update and what we executed: 

What we did (10:00–10:01 PST):
- Performed regional quarantine for Wakefield traffic in us-west-2 (controlled stop for new routed sessions into affected mesh).
- Rerouted new requests to us-east-1 via priority routing pin for your account. Current traffic shift: ~78% rerouted; 22% still hitting legacy sessions while we drain.
- Conducted KV cache priming for hot prefixes to reduce cold-start penalty.

Early results: error rate on your /v1/generate routes reduced from 18% → 3.4% within 6 minutes of the shift; median latency increased ~90ms for routed calls but 95th percentile latency and error rates improved substantially.

Next steps:
- Continue draining remaining legacy sessions (target 30 minutes).
- Follow up with a PSR (post-incident summary) and proposed 10% credit for the affected window.
- We'll run additional load checks to verify no residual capacity contention in us-east-1.

We're keeping this thread open for updates and I'll drop the mitigation logs as we progress. Let me know if you want a brief call.

— Ava
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: traffic_shift_manifest.csv (text)]

— Rishi
